title: Amber Release Manifest (v1)
description: R-ET-5 (0175): the versions a ValidationReceipt binds — what the run validated, not just whether it passed. Frozen into the receipt at write time; integrity is the re-derivation of that stored snapshot, never a comparison against current artifacts (R-ET-5.3 — that question belongs to the separate staleness check). An axis Amber has no record point for is declared null, never omitted and never fabricated.

code.description: The repository the run was validated against: its package version and HEAD commit. Both null when the target carries neither.

task.description: The task the run subject names, and the admitted contract that governed it (id + the Snapshot Hash ADR-0100 froze at admission).

evaluator.description: The bound eval-result revision, reusing the F077 {identity, revision} pin verbatim — null when the validation bound no evaluator. The result's own verdict stays on the receipt's eval check; this axis names WHAT was bound, never how it judged.

provider.description: The EFFECTIVE boundary the run executed under (R-ET-1 / ADR-0104) — the provider's enforcement level, never the declared one. Null on both axes when the run never prepared an execution.

model.description: Always null: Amber has no model introspection — the standing residual replay-core's `model-drift` kind names. The axis is present so the absence is DECLARED (never read as forgotten), and no code path may fill it from a hash or a guess.
